summary: Rob Smyth's live over-by-over report on the fifth and deciding T20 international between West Indies and England at Tarouba. England were bowled out for 132, and West Indies chased it down by 4 wickets with Shai Hope's run-a-ball 43 anchoring the innings, winning the series 3-2. Jos Buttler called the batting a failure to adapt, while the report looks ahead to next year's World Cup.
one_line: West Indies beat England by 4 wickets in the deciding fifth T20I at Tarouba, chasing 133 to win the series 3-2.
key_facts: West Indies won the fifth and deciding T20 international by 4 wickets, finishing on 133-6 after 19.2 overs, to take the series 3-2.
Shai Hope sealed the win by hitting Chris Woakes over extra cover for six; he scored a calm, run-a-ball 43.
England were bowled out for 132 after being 109 for four after 14 overs; Sam Curran was the last man out, caught Rutherford b Holder for 12.
Two days earlier at Tarouba, England had scored 267-3 with 19 sixes; on Thursday they made 132 all out with five sixes.
The winning six was the 120th of the series.
Adil Rashid finished with figures of 4-0-21-2 and took eight wickets at 15 in the series, with an economy rate of 6.26.
Johnson Charles made 27 before being caught by Jos Buttler off Rashid; Sherfane Rutherford made 30 from 23 balls before Curran caught him off Rashid.
Reece Topley dismissed Brandon King (3) and Rovman Powell (8); Woakes bowled Nicholas Pooran for 10.
Andre Russell was caught by Liam Livingstone at long-on off Sam Curran for 3, leaving West Indies needing 10 from 7 balls.
West Indies won a hat-trick of T20 series this year: South Africa away, then India and England at home.
Jos Buttler said England did not adapt quickly enough with the bat, felt 160 would have been decent on a used wicket, and praised Phil Salt's brilliant series.
Rob Smyth wrote that England's white-ball year ended with another series defeat, with a few slots to fill, most notably at No3, ahead of next year's World Cup.
